answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by binding each identity to a single unforgeable proof of work and making that proof the login signal for every action. Cloned identities cannot share one proof, so a farm must mint a separate costly proof per fake; instead, a violet flag marks a verified identity, and unverified clones are denied a seat at the reward inlet. Each new identity also stakes a deposit that it forfeits if the network detects it farming across many addresses, so duplicating an identity costs more than the rewards it could ever harvest.
